opus.why: A short recall of standard ADR sections and when you can skip one. Common knowledge with no reasoning or tools needed.

fable.why: Short recall of standard ADR sections and when to skip one; no tools, no judgment beyond common knowledge.

opus.why: Writes one ADR in the repo's existing format and changes two status fields. The decision is already fully specified, so the work is mostly reading the format, then writing and editing.

fable.why: Well-specified doc task: read existing ADRs to match format, write one with given decision, flip two statuses. Routine agentic editing.

opus.why: Designing a ledger schema with append-only entries, reversals, 12-month expiry and FIFO partial redemption, plus migrating balances that have no history. The data-model choices are subtle and expensive to redo later.

fable.why: Data-model redesign (append-only ledger, FIFO batches, expiry, balance strategy, migration) that must not need rework later; schema mistakes are costly.

opus.why: An architecture tradeoff call (Kafka vs RabbitMQ vs outbox) under concrete constraints. Needs judgment more than deep multi-step work.

fable.why: Judgment-heavy infra recommendation with real tradeoffs for team size and scale; shallow comparison is exactly what the user rejects.

opus.why: Decides whether a module boundary is actually leaking and plans the public interface and repository ownership. Contained code reading, but the architectural judgment matters.

fable.why: Module-boundary analysis needing repo exploration and a proposed public interface for onboarding; architectural judgment where errors mislead the refactor.

opus.why: Target architecture for a multi-agent pipeline: stages, handoff formats, retries, cost caps and resume-from-failure. Open-ended systems design with many interacting decisions.

fable.why: Target architecture for a multi-agent render pipeline with handoff formats, retries, cost caps and resume; complex system design with many interacting decisions.

opus.why: Turns an agreed design into a phased Jira plan with risks, a cutover strategy and a list of what not to do in phase 1. The design already exists, but sequencing and risk judgment still matter.

fable.why: Continues the notification-service design: phased migration plan with parallelism, risks, strangler cutover and what to avoid; planning quality drives real work.

opus.why: Design-token architecture: Style Dictionary vs a custom script, tier naming, versioning. Well-established practice and the user wants it brief, so Sonnet at high matches.

fable.why: Design-token tooling question with well-established answers (Style Dictionary, primitive/semantic/component tiers, versioning); needs a concise opinionated reply, not frontier reasoning.

opus.why: Compares Konsist, ArchUnit and detekt, maps 10 ADRs to whichever tool can check each one, says what can't be automated, and proposes a naming convention linking each test to its ADR. Research plus architecture judgment.

fable.why: Research across three tools plus repo inspection, mapping each ADR to enforceability and proposing a naming convention; architecture governance decision needing careful judgment.
